text:
The Panthers were down 4-1 in the second period and still won. Florida came back from three goals down to beat Detroit 5-4, and the Red Wings are now winless in five (0-5-0).

Detroit's early lead came from some unlikely places. Andreas Englund scored on a shot our numbers gave a 2% chance, and Lucas Raymond and Marco Kasper added goals before the second period was half over. Gustav Forsling cut it to 4-2 in the final seconds of the second, and from there it was a one-sided game. Florida's expected goals (a measure of how good its chances were) in the third period were 2.66 to Detroit's 0.79. Anton Lundell, the first star, made it 4-3 early in the period, and Lars Eller tied it with a deflection off his bat on a 73% chance. Lundell scored again 51 seconds later, on an 82% chance, for the winner. Lundell was the 12th pick in 2020 out of HIFK in Finland, and he finished with both of those goals. Carter Verhaeghe, picked 82nd by Toronto in 2013, added three assists.

Over 60 minutes, our numbers say Florida deserved to win 74% of the time, meaning it takes the game in about three of every four simulated replays of every shot. The Panthers out-attempted Detroit 63 to 46 and led in expected goals 4.36 to 2.90, yet the shots on goal were nearly even, 29 to 28. Both goalies finished below expectation: Akira Schmid allowed 1.1 goals more than his shots deserved, and John Gibson 0.64 more. Detroit had won the first meeting between the teams 5-3 on Nov. 2.

The Panthers took the comeback and the points, while Detroit has now blown a three-goal lead on its way to a fifth straight winless night.
